extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners, and USPTO examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Procedures and substantive requirements for (1) petitions to revive abandoned or lapsed patent applications/patents under 37 CFR 1.137, and (2) petitions to withdraw a holding of abandonment under 37 CFR 1.181, including evidence, fees, terminal disclaimer rules, timing, and special situations that cause abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to revive under 37 CFR 1.137(a) (unavoidable delay)
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition to revive an abandoned application on the grounds that the failure to reply was unavoidable must be accompanied by: (1) the required reply (unless previously filed); (2) the petition fee as set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(l); (3) a showing to the satisfaction of the Director that the entire delay in filing the required reply from the due date until filing the petition was unavoidable; and (4) any terminal disclaimer required pursuant to 37 CFR 1.137(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No consideration to the substance of a petition will be given until the fee is received. The Director may require additional information where there is a question whether the delay was unavoidable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to revive under 37 CFR 1.137(b) (unintentional delay)
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition to revive on grounds that the failure to reply was unintentional must be accompanied by: (1) the required reply (unless previously filed); (2) the petition fee as set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(m); (3) a statement that the entire delay from the due date until filing the petition was unintentional; and (4) any terminal disclaimer required pursuant to 37 CFR 1.137(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director may require additional information where there is a question whether the delay was unintentional. The required statement must cover the entire delay period. No consideration is given until the fee is received.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply requirement for petitions under 37 CFR 1.137 (37 CFR 1.137(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: The petition must be accompanied by the 'required reply' which, generally, is the reply sufficient to have avoided abandonment had it been timely filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In a nonprovisional application abandoned for failure to prosecute, the required reply may be met by filing a continuing application; in a nonprovisional utility or plant application filed on or after June 8, 1995, by filing an RCE in compliance with 37 CFR 1.114; for abandonment or lapse due to failure to pay an issue fee or publication fee, the required reply must include payment of the issue or publication fee (or any outstanding balance). A petition for an extension of time under 37 CFR 1.136 is not required to be included with the reply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer requirement for revival (37 CFR 1.137(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain petitions to revive must be accompanied by a terminal disclaimer dedicating to the public a terminal part of the patent term equivalent to the period of abandonment (and applicable fee).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design applications, utility applications filed before June 8, 1995, and plant applications filed before June 8, 1995 require a terminal disclaimer dedicating the terminal part equivalent to the period of abandonment. For pre-1995 utility/plant apps the period to disclaim is the lesser of (i) the period of abandonment or (ii) the period extending beyond 20 years from the filing date (or earliest 35 U.S.C. 120/121/365(c) priority date). The terminal disclaimer must also apply to patents on continuing applications that contain a specific reference to the application for which revival is sought. Exceptions: revival sought solely for copendency with a post-June 8, 1995 application, lapsed patents, reissue apps, or reexaminations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to withdraw holding of abandonment under 37 CFR 1.181 (when appropriate)
rubrics_metrics.description: When applicant contends the application is not in fact abandoned (e.g., disagreement as to sufficiency of the reply or controlling dates), a petition under 37 CFR 1.181(a) requesting withdrawal of the holding of abandonment is appropriate and does not require a fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is distinct from a petition to revive under 37 CFR 1.137, which is used when there is no dispute that the application is abandoned. The mere filing of a petition does not stay any period for reply. Petitions under this part not filed within two months of the mailing date of the action or notice may be dismissed as untimely; the two-month period is not extendable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence required to establish nonreceipt of Office action (petition to withdraw holding of abandonment)
rubrics_metrics.description: To establish nonreceipt of an Office communication, the showing must include: a practitioner statement that the Office communication was not received and attesting that a search of the file jacket and docket indicates the Office communication was not received; and a copy of the docket record where the nonreceived communication would have been entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: if a three-month reply period was set, include the docket report showing replies docketed for a date three months from the mail date as documentary proof. The showing may be insufficient if circumstances suggest the action was lost after receipt (e.g., practitioner has a history of not receiving Office actions). Evidence of nonreceipt of other communications (not the one to which reply was required) generally does not warrant withdrawal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof via mailing methods: Express Mail, postcard receipt, certificate of mailing (timely filing evidence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Express Mail procedures under 37 CFR 1.10(c)-(e)/(g) may be used to accord a filing date as of deposit. A postcard receipt properly identifying the reply provides prima facie evidence the reply was timely filed. A certificate of mailing under 37 CFR 1.8, with the required personal-knowledge statement (or equivalent supporting evidence), may also be relied upon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When shown mailed by Express Mail, the paper must be entered in PALM with the Express Mail date. If relying on a postcard receipt, entry into PALM uses the date on the postcard. For certificate of mailing, the attesting statement must be on personal knowledge basis or include supporting evidence (e.g., mailing log). If a duplicate copy plus statement under 1.8(b)(3) is submitted after reasonable time has elapsed, the correspondence is entered into PALM with the actual date of receipt (the duplicate filing date).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing limits and effects for replies, extensions, and abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant's reply must reach the Office within the shortened statutory period from the date stamped or printed on the Office letter or within the extended time under 37 CFR 1.136. The date the petition under 1.136(a) and the extension fee are filed governs the period of extension and corresponding fee; no reply may be filed outside the six-month statutory period or obtain more than five months extension beyond the date for reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A fully responsive reply must be timely filed to avoid abandonment. If a reply appears to be a bona fide attempt with an inadvertent omission, use alternative form paragraph (7.95) rather than the 'not fully responsive' paragraph (7.91).

rubrics_metrics.name: Situations that commonly cause abandonment (insufficiency or timing issues)
rubrics_metrics.description: Abandonment may result when a reply is within the period but not fully responsive; copying claims from a patent when not suggested by the Office does not constitute a reply unless the Office relied solely on the patent; abandonment can result from withdrawal/failure to prosecute appeals, dismissal of appeals/court action without timely amendment, interference-related issues, improper RCE/CPA filings, or failure to pay issue/publication fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP sections cited for each situation (e.g., §710, §714, §1215, §706.07(h)). Specific examples: (A) copying claims from a patent doesn't save app unless last action based solely on the patent; (B)-(G) list appeal/interference/RCE/CPA/issue fee related abandonment examples. Improper RCE filings will not toll periods and may be treated as withdrawal of appeal or not prevent abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of untimely petitions to withdraw the holding of abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 37 CFR 1.181(f), petitions not filed within two months from the action complained of may be dismissed as untimely. Rather than dismissing an untimely petition, the Office may require a terminal disclaimer as a condition of granting the petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special rules apply for certain application types: design apps and pre-June-8-1995 utility/plant apps—if applicant receives notice, any petition not filed within two months will not be treated on its merits unless accompanied by a terminal disclaimer; if applicant never received notice, untimely petition not filed within 12 months of the applicant's filing/submission (for which further Office action could be expected) will not be treated on its merits absent terminal disclaimer. Form PTO/SB/62 is the terminal disclaimer form to use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special rules by filing date/category for terminal disclaimers when granting untimely petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: For design apps, pre-June-8-1995 utility/plant apps special terminal-disclaimer rules apply if petition to withdraw is untimely. For utility/plant apps filed on or after June 8, 1995 but before May 29, 2000, a terminal disclaimer should not be required but OPLA consultation is needed if holding involves certain periods (appellate review, interference, secrecy orders). For apps filed on or after May 29, 2000, terminal disclaimer should not be required because AIPA patent term adjustment rules automatically reduce PTA for failure to engage in reasonable efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where record indicates intentional delay by applicant in filing petition to withdraw, the Office may dismiss petition as untimely without addressing merits. Intentional delay precludes relief under 37 CFR 1.137(a) or (b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Revival for failure to pay issue or publication fee (separate statutory basis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Revival of applications abandoned for failure to pay the issue fee or publication fee is governed by statutory provisions (35 U.S.C. 151 and 35 U.S.C. 41(a)(7)); payment of the issue fee (or outstanding balance) is a condition of reviving an application abandoned or a patent lapsed for failure to pay the issue fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing a continuing application without payment of the issue fee is not acceptable reply in an application abandoned or patent lapsed for failure to pay the issue fee. If issue fee increased after Notice of Allowance, Office will require payment of balance. For publication-fee abandonment, required reply must include payment of the publication fee even if revival is sought solely for continuity with a continuing application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconsideration by examiner of holding of abandonment (insufficiency or date disputes)
rubrics_metrics.description: The primary examiner has no authority to act upon an application in which no action was taken during the period for reply, but may reverse his/her holding as to whether an amendment received during such period was responsive and then act on the application—this is not a revival but a holding that the application was never abandoned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When amendment reaches the Office after expiration of the period and dates are undisputed, no reconsideration can be presented. If examiner and applicant disagree as to dates, applicant may take issue and request withdrawal of the holding. See MPEP §714.03 for related guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitions to the Director (37 CFR 1.181) — scope and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition may be taken to the Director from any action/requirement of any examiner in ex parte prosecution (when not subject to appeal to the Board), when statute or rules specify direct determination by the Director, or to invoke supervisory authority of the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing a petition does not stay any period for reply or other proceedings. Petitions not filed within two months of the mailing date of the action or notice may be dismissed as untimely; this two-month period is not extendable. For petitions involving Board actions see §41.3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revival of provisional applications and pendency limits
rubrics_metrics.description: A provisional application abandoned for failure to timely respond to an Office requirement may be revived pursuant to 37 CFR 1.137, but subject to 35 U.S.C. 119(e)(3) and 37 CFR 1.7(b) a provisional application will not be regarded as pending after twelve months from its filing date under any circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revival procedures apply but do not override the 12-month pendency limitation for provisional applications.
